transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes | Attendees: Sofia Martinez, Devon Li (Redwood); Dr. Priya Nair, Marco Ruiz, Aisha Khan (Orbital MedTech)

Summary: Quick POC scoping between Redwood AE/SE and Orbital MedTech to decide hosting mode for an inference POC: hosted API vs dedicated reserved capacity vs private VPC/on-prem. Discussed success criteria (latency, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy delta), workload sizing (RPS, sequence lengths), benchmark plan and timeline.

Topics: POC goals; baseline performance expectations; security and compliance gating; model choices and quantization; telemetry & SLAs; pilot timeline and responsibilities.

00:00 Sofia: hey everyone uh thanks for joining on time, this is Sofia from Redwood, AE on your account, we also have Devon from our SE team.
00:08 Priya: thanks Sofia, yeah I'm Priya — head of ML at Orbital, Marco and Aisha are on as well. We'll try to keep this focused — we've got an internal exec sync at 4.
00:16 Devon: hi all, quick agenda — align on success criteria for the POC, confirm workload shape, pick candidate models and deployment mode to test, and define the benchmark run and timeline.
00:28 Marco: great. high level — our use case is clinical note summarization and triage routing, about 200k notes/month currently, spiky during rounds, target peak ~15 RPS, tail latency important.
00:41 Aisha: and from security we need SOC2 evidence, KMS-integrations for key material, and VPC peering or private link for the POC — we can't send PHI to a public multi-tenant endpoint without controls.
00:54 Sofia: noted. so first question — do you want to test hosted API or are you leaning towards Dedicated or Private straight away? either is fine for a POC but gating differs.
01:04 Priya: honestly we'd prefer hosted if it can meet latency and security needs, fosters faster iteration. but if hosted can't give the isolation and KMS hooks, we may need Dedicated or Private.
01:14 Devon: right — hosted gives fastest time-to-value. we have transit encryption and customer isolation controls, but for BYO-KMS or full VPC private control, Dedicated or Private is the pattern. there's a gradient: Hosted -> Dedicated (reserved pools + VPC peering option) -> Private (control plane in your VPC or on-prem).
01:33 Marco: can we get a matrix of what features map to which mode? like KMS yes/no, data residency, SLA, throughput guarantees.
01:41 Sofia: yes we'll send that. high level: Hosted = fastest onboarding, no dedicated GPUs, best for variable workloads; Dedicated = reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and can enable VPC networking; Private = everything in your network, audit logs, HSM options, longer lead time and contractual.
01:57 Priya: ok, POC success criteria — what do you recommend? for us: median latency under 400ms for 512-token sequences, 99th under 1.2s, accuracy (f1 / rouge?) within 2% of our baseline, and cost per processed note under $0.02. thoughts?
02:15 Devon: those are concrete. a couple of calibration points — model choice and quantization will impact latency and accuracy. if you want top quality, we suggest a fp16 or bf16 variant of the open model; for lower cost, int8 or q4 variants are possible but expect some small delta in output. we can quantify during the bench.
02:31 Marco: our baseline is a fine-tuned Llama-2 13B (on prem now) — we care a lot about hallucination rates on clinical context. can Redwood host that model in a POC?
02:43 Sofia: yes, we can serve customer-provided models in Dedicated and Private; Hosted can host it too, but licensing/weight upload and private model policy needs signoff, and there are egress and storage considerations. we'll note that.
02:56 Priya: what about continuous batching — our traffic is bursty: long quiet periods then sudden batch ingestion during shift changes. how does batching affect latency SLOs?
03:08 Devon: Redwood runtime supports workload-aware batching and prefix/KV caching. the idea is to keep tail latency bounded by capping batch windows for latency-sensitive routes and use larger batches on background inference. For your 15 RPS peak with spiky bursts, Dedicated gives more control over autoscaling policies and guaranteed capacity.
03:25 Aisha: on the encryption/KMS piece — can we bring our own KMS keys and use HSM for inference keys?
03:32 Devon: for Private yes; Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS integrations for model secrets and optionally data. Hosted allows envelope encryption to your KMS in some tiers but not HSM-backed key roles. we'll share an integration matrix.
03:45 Marco: benchmarks — what does Redwood need from us to run a meaningful benchmark?
03:50 Devon: sample dataset (anonymized), a traffic profile (RPS distribution, sequence length histogram), and success metric definitions (latency percentiles, token cost, accuracy eval set). We'll run three configurations: hosted baseline (if allowed), Dedicated with reserved pool, and Private sim with the same model/config if available.
04:09 Priya: timeline? we have a compliance board meeting in two weeks; ideally POC results before end of month. is that realistic?
04:16 Sofia: for a minimal bench we can do a two-week cycle: day 1-3 setup and model onboarding, day 4-8 run perf sweeps and calibrate, day 9-11 accuracy/eval and stability, day 12-14 report and review. Private setup may add lead time (provisioning VPC appliances or packaging on-prem) — expect extra 1-2 weeks.
04:35 Marco: ok. cost — can you ballpark delta hosted vs dedicated?
04:40 Sofia: rough rules: hosted = pay per token + lower commitment, Dedicated = monthly reserved instance(s) so unit cost goes down at scale but you commit, Private = license + infra ops so higher fixed cost but best for compliance and predictable at enterprise scale. We'll include a simple cost model based on your 200k notes/month and target latency.
04:58 Aisha: audit logs retention? we need 12 months for compliance.
05:02 Devon: observability and audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private with configurable retention; hosted has shorter retention but we have add-on packages for extended logs.
05:12 Priya: model quality — we need to quantify 'within 2%' — what's the evaluation harness look like?
05:18 Devon: we'll run an eval suite you provide — compute standard metrics (ROUGE/F1, hallucination spot checks). We'll produce a diff vs your baseline and also log tokenization differences. if quantization introduces degradation we'll show sample cases.
05:30 Marco: network topology — if we go Dedicated, how do we handle VPC peering and egress?
05:35 Sofia: Dedicated supports VPC peering, Private supports fully private control plane and on-prem. Egress policies can be restricted and we can set up private link for data path. We'll coordinate networking details during setup.
05:48 Aisha: what about failover and graceful degradation? in production we need fallback to smaller models or cached responses.
05:55 Devon: Redwood has smart routing and fallback policies — you can define route preference: primary = high-quality model on Dedicated, fallback = hosted lightweight quantized model or cached summary. We'll demo policymapping in the console during the pilot.
06:08 Priya: any red flags for us if we wanted to start with Hosted but have security needs?
06:14 Sofia: the main constraint is KMS/HSM and specific network isolation. If Aisha's team can accept envelope encryption and strict access controls, hosted is a good quick start. If not, Dedicated is the pragmatic middle ground.
06:25 Marco: ok, bench specifics — can you outline the exact metrics we'll get in the report?
06:29 Devon: yes: median/95/99 latency per input length bucket, throughput (RPS sustained), tokens/sec per GPU, cost per 1k tokens, memory and CPU usage, model cache hit rates, and accuracy metrics from your eval set. We'll also produce a regression alert matrix if quality drops beyond thresholds.
06:46 Priya: and for models — do you recommend Llama-2 13B fp16 or an open LLM-34B?
06:51 Devon: Llama-2 13B is a good start; 34B gives better quality but higher latency & cost. We'll run both if you want to compare — but that'll increase bench time and cost.
07:03 Aisha: compliance question — can logs be SAML/audit-linked to our SSO users?
07:09 Sofia: yes, we can map tokens to identities and connect audit logs to your SSO identities for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has role-based tokens but limited identity mapping out of the box.
07:20 Marco: ok, let's scope the POC to two parallel runs: 1) Hosted quick-run with a redwood-managed endpoint (if permitted) using a 13B q4 model to get baseline latency/cost, and 2) Dedicated reserved pool running your 13B fp16 fine-tuned model with VPC peering. If needed, we'll do Private as a later follow-up.
07:41 Priya: sounds good. we need to ensure PHI constraints are met for the hosted run — Aisha will confirm acceptance or veto.
07:49 Aisha: yes I'll confirm; my default is restrictive but if hosted run can be limited to synthetic/anonymized dataset, that might be okay.
07:57 Sofia: perfect. action items and owners — we'll capture these in the follow-up email.
08:03 Devon: technical note — for the Dedicated run we'll provide a containerized runtime and a benchmark harness. please provide a small sample of clinical notes and a short eval set. We'll also include instructions for how to reproduce the bench locally.
08:17 Marco: what's the expected token billing for the hosted quick run?
08:20 Sofia: depends on length; rough estimate: if average note is 600 tokens incoming and response 150 tokens, that's ~750 tokens per request; at your volume for the bench we'll calculate exact. We'll include a cost table.
08:34 Priya: timeline recap — we want reports before EOM; bench kickoff next week?
08:38 Sofia: yes — propose kickoff 2025-12-08, bench run 12-09 through 12-12, and review on 12-15. We'll align dates in follow-up.
08:48 Aisha: please include SOC2 scoping docs and any third-party pen-test reports.
08:52 Sofia: will do.
08:55 Marco: small question — does Redwood support deploying model updates mid-bench to test rollouts?
08:59 Devon: yes — we support canary rollouts and traffic splitting, but for fair benching we usually freeze the model variant per run then run a separate incremental test for rollouts.
09:12 Priya: great. any other blocking items?
09:15 Aisha: none from me besides the hosted PHI check.
09:18 Marco: none.
09:20 Sofia: ok we'll send the pricing matrix, qualifying matrix of features by deployment mode, benchmark harness, and the kickoff calendar invite.
09:28 Priya: thanks everyone.
09:30 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: some names or product names may be transcribed slightly off (e.g., references to KV cache, VPC, KMS spelled out or mis-cased). There is a bit of overlapping speech around the 02:00-03:00 mark.

Attachments/refs mentioned: "deployment-mode-matrix.pdf" (to be shared), "benchmark-harness.zip" (Devon to share), SOC2 summary link (to be provided).

Recap & explicit next steps (captured in next_steps metadata): - Redwood to send hosting feature matrix and sample pricing by 2025-12-04. - Customer to confirm whether anonymized data is acceptable for hosted quick-run by 2025-12-05. - SE to share benchmark scripts and container by 2025-12-06. - Kickoff meeting scheduled week of 2025-12-08 (TBD).
